rationale: The hypothesis posits a specific quantitative finding: that within the dominant cohort of 35 patients reported by Leitão et al. (2026), episodic central hyperventilation (HP:0002883) was documented in 35% to 60% (12 to 21 individuals). While hyperventilation is recognized as a recurrent feature of dominant RNU2-2 encephalopathy in smaller series (e.g., Chiu et al. 2026 observed it in 3 of 5 patients, and Krygier et al. 2026 noted hyperventilation episodes preceding seizures), the Leitão et al. (2026) study does not report this phenotype or provide evidence for this frequency in their 35 dominant cases. Under adversarial testing, attributing this specific 35-60% frequency to the Leitão et al. cohort is unsupported and refuted by the provided source record.

evidence.text: Leitão et al. analyzed 141 individuals with RNU2-2 variants, including 35 with recurrent dominant pathogenic variants, but the provided publication text and abstract do not report episodic central hyperventilation or document it in 12 to 21 (35% to 60%) of these 35 dominant individuals.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: Here, through international collaborations, we analyze systematically 200 potentially functional snRNA genes in a French cohort of 34,329 people with rare disorders. We report RNU2-2 variants in 141 individuals, including 35 with recurrent dominant pathogenic variants and 91 affected members from 73 families with biallelic variants.

evidence.text: Chiu et al. (2026) described clinical findings in 5 patients with dominant RNU2-2 DEE, observing hyperventilation in 3 of 5 individuals (60%), alongside status epilepticus in 5 of 5, obstructive sleep apnea in 3 of 5, and hippocampal sclerosis in 3.

source.title: Pathogenic Variants in RNU2‐2, a Non‐coding Spliceosomal RNA, Cause a Distinctive Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy
source.quote: Patients with RNU2-2 DEE had median seizure onset age of 24 months, focal and generalized seizures, status epilepticus (n = 5), severe to profound impairment, hyperventilation (n = 3), and obstructive sleep apnea (n = 3).

conflicts: The hypothesis asserts a specific prevalence of 35% to 60% (12 to 21 of 35 individuals) in the Leitão et al. cohort, but Leitão et al. (2026) contains no documentation of episodic central hyperventilation frequencies in their dominant cohort.

Reported frequencies of hyperventilation derive from the small cohort in Chiu et al. (n = 3/5, 60%) and qualitative reports in Krygier et al. (2026), rather than systematic documentation across larger multicenter cohorts like Leitão et al.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of episodic hyperventilation across all aggregated dominant RNU2-2 DEE cohorts when standardized HPO phenotyping is applied?
new_directions.rationale: While small initial case series (Chiu et al., Krygier et al.) highlight hyperventilation as a potential discriminator (seen in 3/5 patients), systematically capturing this finding across larger registries is needed to establish its true sensitivity and positive predictive value relative to other DEEs.

new_directions.question_text: Does episodic hyperventilation occur in biallelic (recessive) RNU2-2 neurodevelopmental disorders, or is it exclusive to dominant de novo cases?
new_directions.rationale: Recent publications demonstrate that recessive RNU2-2 syndrome is clinically and mechanistically distinct from dominant RNU2-2 DEE; establishing whether autonomic respiratory dysfunction is unique to dominant cases will aid clinical differentiation.
